 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna
 Order

Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.153/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Palam Village, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 18.04.2009 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
There is no child from this wedlock.

However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple started living separately from each other since 27.01.2015 and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 also filed the criminal complaint cases under Section 125 Cr PC and Section 12 of the DV Act against the petitioner vNo.1
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 22.09.2022.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent.

Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 agreed to pay Rs.3.60 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc, which amount has already been received by respondent No.2 and nothing is left due against any of the petitioners.

3. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
5. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Consequently, FIR No.153/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Palam Village, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
